_comment: Mutation testing acts as a third reviewer of the tester/implementer contract: it mutates production behaviour and asks whether the accepted tests notice. The scope is deliberately small and deterministic to start — two pure utilities with dedicated suites — because a first run is diagnostic, not a gate. Widen it once a baseline exists. Browser automation, network paths, IMAP loops and worker threads are excluded on purpose: they are slow, environment-heavy, and their behaviour is pinned by the locked integration suites instead.
_ignoreComment: Stryker copies the project into a sandbox. .claude/skills is a symlink mirror (see .gitignore) and copying symlinks fails with EPERM on Windows; the rest is bulk that slows every sandbox copy without being mutated or imported.
_runnerNote: The Bun-specific Stryker runner (@hughescr/stryker-bun-runner) was trialled and rejected: it strips backslashes from the Windows project path (Cannot find package D:Projectsmkfd) and times out fetching Bun inspector URL. It also pulled smol-toml 1.7.0 (CVSS 8.2). The built-in command runner loses per-test coverage and selectivity, which is why each mutant re-runs the four suites below, but it works on both supported platforms.
